title: Semantics of a decrement instruction
statement: Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program, $O$ an oracle family, $x$ an input bit string, and $G$ a guard on configurations. Suppose the instruction at state $l$ decrements register $r$ (with subtraction truncated at zero) and proceeds to state $l'$. If $G$ holds at $(l,v,\mathrm{none})$, then for any proposition $P$, terminating semantics and acceptance equivalent to $P$ at $(l',v',\mathrm{none})$, where $v'(r)=\max(v(r)-1,0)$ and all other register values agree with $v$, imply the same semantics at $(l,v,\mathrm{none})$.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at $l$ decrements register $r$ and proceeds to $l'$
The successor configuration uses the decremented value $v(r)-1$ with natural-number truncated subtraction and has terminating semantics and acceptance equivalent to $P$
